title: Build an Array With Stack Operations
description:
You are given a strictly increasing integer array `target` and an integer `n`.

You have an empty stack and a stream of integers `[1, 2, ..., n]` read in ascending order. Use the following two operations to make the stack (from bottom to top) equal to `target`:
- `"Push"`: read the next integer from the stream and push it onto the stack.
- `"Pop"`: remove the integer on the top of the stack.

Once the stack equals `target`, stop reading immediately and do not perform any further operations. Return the list of stack operations needed to build `target`.
hints: For every stream integer from 1 up to target[-1], you must always emit 'Push'.
If the stream integer is not the next needed element in target, immediately emit 'Pop'; otherwise advance the pointer in target.

examples.explanation: Push 1 (keep), Push 2 then Pop 2 (skip), Push 3 (keep) produces [1, 3].
Push 1 and 2 produces [1, 2]; stop immediately without reading 3 or 4.
